newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Apr 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Apr 14.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- WEN WEI PO -- China announced details of permanent residency after the July 1 handover. Non-Chinese Hong Kong residents would lose their permanent residency rights if they did not reside in the territory for more than three years.

-- APPLE DAILY -- Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa's office is considering speeding up the timetable for mainland children of Hong Kong parents to reunify with their family in the territory after the handover.
-- MING PAO -- The head of Hopewell Holdings Ltd, Gordon Wu, said massive land reclamation was the way forward for Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa to resolve property problems in Hong Kong.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Public confidence in Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa has dropped amid concern over proposed curbs on civil liberties, according to a poll commissioned by the South China Morning Post.
-- The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong's ruling council is set for a major shake-up, with chairman Edgar Cheng Wai-kin and 15 members of the council due to step down in October.
